habitat: Singly or in pairs in woodland, riverine forest, mixed bushveld and thornveld, preferring drier regions with large trees. In some years it moves into suburban areas.
summary: A common resident. The largest of the small owls. It is predominantly grey, with orange eyes, a white facial disc outlined in black, ear tufts and fine black streaking below. The call, heard only at night, is an explosive bubbling b-b-b-b-b-bhooo. The Kemp name Whitefaced Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.

head.pattern: White facial disc with a broad black outline, and ear tufts. The bird is predominantly grey.

underparts.pattern: Fine black streaking on the underparts.

viewNotes.note: Orange eyes and a white facial disc with a broad black outline.
Predominantly grey, with ear tufts and fine black streaking below.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: An explosive bubbling 'b-b-b-b-b-bhooo', heard only at night. At a distance only the 'bhooo' is audible. The grade A files are typed as song, not call. The selected file is from Namibia. No Kruger recording was found. The filename is XC1059179-MixPre-925_Ptilopsis-granti_YB.wav.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The grade A recordings are typed as song. No Kruger recording was found. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login joao_marcelo_da_costa is credited. The Kemp name Whitefaced Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.
